name: Zara Keomanivong
role: Gene-mod body artist and tattoo artist
location: Mexicantown Libre, shop called Dermis Atlas, near Western and Division
description:
Zara Keomanivong is compact and restless, with the kind of energy that makes a small room feel occupied. She has Polynesian-Hungarian heritage written clearly across her features — broad cheekbones, dark eyes with a slight upward tilt, medium-brown skin covered from collarbones to wrists in her own work, a living portfolio that shifts slowly across the seasons because half her ink is bioluminescent and the other half is geneware-reactive, changing saturation with her mood. Her hair is close-cropped on the sides and grown long on top, currently dyed a deep oxidized copper that she changes every three months. A single cosmetic cat ear — just one, the left — sits atop her head, rose-gold and slightly translucent, a signature affectation she has maintained since she was nineteen.

She runs Dermis Atlas out of a converted ground-floor space in Mexicantown Libre, its walls covered in design sketches and photographs of completed work. Her specialty is narrative tattooing — pieces that tell a client's specific story using symbols drawn from their actual heritage, their personal mythology, their body's own geneware reactions. She refuses flash designs entirely and has a six-month waitlist she refuses to shorten for money. She is warm to clients in a professional way, genuinely curious about their lives, and fiercely opinionated about the difference between body art and body modification as commodity — a distinction she will explain at length to anyone who triggers it.

core_fears: Losing the precision in her hands — any injury that ends her ability to work
Becoming the kind of artist who makes things for money rather than meaning
core_desires: To map every story she hears onto skin and preserve it permanently
To be recognized not as a craftsperson but as an artist — a distinction that matters enormously to her
coping_mechanisms: The secret Tuesday paintings that nobody sees
Elaborate pre-session rituals involving specific music and a particular brand of synthetic tea
blind_spots: Her insistence on narrative authenticity sometimes means she imposes her interpretation of a client's story over their actual wishes
She undervalues the work of artists who work faster or more commercially than her
psychology.secret: The large-format paintings she makes on Tuesdays are increasingly disturbing — violent, chaotic, nothing like her controlled professional work. She doesn't understand why she makes them and is frightened by what they might mean about her interior state. She has started making offerings to the E.L.F. she believes inhabits her ink-mixing station, asking it to interpret the paintings for her.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Articulate and opinionated, mixes technical body-art terminology with unexpectedly poetic descriptions of people and places
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when excited, deliberate when making a point she considers important — the shift is noticeable
verbal_tics: Touches her cat ear absently when thinking
example_lines: 'Your skin is the only thing that goes everywhere you go for your entire life. Why would you put something meaningless on it?'
'I'm not tattooing you. I'm writing a sentence about you that you'll carry for the rest of your life. That takes time to get right.'

story_hooks: A client she tattooed six months ago has disappeared, and the last message they sent her contained a fragment of something coded — she doesn't know what it means but can't stop thinking about it
A rival body artist has been copying her signature techniques and marketing them as original work; Inessa wants redress but the rival has corporate backing
The geneware ink supplier she has used for eight years has suddenly gone dark — no messages, no shipments — and the replacement supplier's product is behaving in ways she's never seen before
narrative_function: Information hub and community connector — her clients tell her everything; quest giver when a client's story pulls her into something larger; can provide access to Mexicantown Libre's deeper community networks
augmentations: Extensive bioluminescent and geneware-reactive tattoo coverage (her own work and others'); single cosmetic cat ear (left, rose-gold, fully sensory); precision haptic fingertip pads on both hands for fine line work; color-shifting irises (purple-to-gold spectrum, mood-reactive)
daily_life: Opens Dermis Atlas at midday and works until late evening, spending mornings designing client pieces and sourcing geneware inks; takes Tuesdays completely offline, no clients, no messages — she spends them painting large-format works she never shows anyone.
affiliation: Independent; member of the Mexicantown Libre Artists' Cooperative

decision_rules: Never rush a design — if it isn't right, it isn't done
Protect clients' stories as confidential even under social pressure
Never work on someone who seems coerced or afraid
escalation_ladder: Direct statement of her position with explanation
Firm refusal and request to leave
Banning from the premises with notification to the Cooperative

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally warm and curious — asks a lot of questions about them before offering anything about herself
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unguarded, opinionated, generous with time and resources, occasionally overwhelming in her enthusiasm

stress_responses.low: Adds extra detail to whatever she's working on
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and businesslike, drops the warmth
stress_responses.high: Cancels everything and paints in the back room until she can regulate

contradictions: She believes deeply in client autonomy but struggles to let go of her own vision for their piece once she's committed to a design
habits: Burns a specific synthetic resin before every session as an offering to the ink-station E.L.F.
Photographs every completed piece from the same angle with the same lighting, catalogued obsessively
breaking_points: Anyone touching her work materials without permission
Being told her work is 'just tattooing'

2185 — Apprentices under a traditional tattoo artist in the Cooperative at age sixteen
2190 — Opens Dermis Atlas at twenty-one with borrowed funds from the Cooperative
2195 — Develops geneware-reactive ink technique, waitlist begins
2199 — Tuesday paintings begin; grows increasingly disturbed by their content

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Sub-Saharan African (39.5%) with significant Southeast Asian (22.8%) and South Asian (17.1%) ancestry, complemented by Northern European (10.3%) and Hispanic/Latin American (10.3%) admixture. This rare combination produces rich warm brown skin with golden and subtle reddish undertones, creating a complex and luminous complexion. The blending produces a striking synthesis: broader facial structure and fuller features from Sub-Saharan African genetics; almond-shaped eyes with Southeast Asian characteristics; high, defined cheekbones from South Asian ancestry; fine bone structure refined by Northern European contribution; and warm undertones enhanced by Hispanic/Latin American heritage.
physical_description.build: Compact and wiry, with the coiled restlessness of someone who rarely sits still. Defined shoulders and forearms from years of precision handiwork; minimal body fat; posture suggests contained kinetic energy.
physical_description.hair_color: Deep oxidized copper (chemically dyed, naturally black)
physical_description.hair_style: Undercut: close-cropped shaved sides with longer growth on crown, typically styled swept to one side or pulled back loosely
physical_description.hair_length: Medium (long on top, short on sides)
physical_description.eye_color: Color-shifting irises: purple-to-gold spectrum, reactive to emotional state and lighting conditions
physical_description.skin_tone: Rich warm brown with golden and subtle reddish undertones, reflecting the dominant Sub-Saharan African ancestry beautifully blended with Southeast Asian and South Asian warmth, tempered by cool Northern European undertones
physical_description.complexion: Clear, even skin with a lived-in quality. Fuller facial structure with high, defined cheekbones; almond-shaped eyes with natural slight upward tilt; broader nose bridge from African heritage; fine but substantial facial bone structure synthesizing multiple ancestral lines. Face shows focus and intensity; minimal cosmetic grooming beyond functional maintenance. Calm resting expression with quick, sharp micro-expressions when engaged.
distinguishing_marks: Extensive bioluminescent tattoo coverage across collarbone, chest, shoulders, and both forearms — intricate narrative designs in blues, greens, and purples that glow faintly in low light
Geneware-reactive tattoo work across ribs and left flank that shifts saturation based on mood and body temperature
Layered geometric patterns on both wrists and hands, some her own work, some commissioned from peers — functional art that doubles as a portfolio
Fine-line sacred/personal symbols on the inner aspect of both wrists, rendered in standard black ink with minimal visibility unless arms are raised
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Single rose-gold cosmetic cat ear on left side of head, slightly translucent with internal LED matrix visible under skin; ear is fully sensory and articulates slightly. Precision haptic fingertip pads on both hands visible as faint raised scar tissue and slightly different texture on fingertips — barely noticeable unless examined closely. Color-shifting iris augs are obvious in conversation, especially in variable lighting.
physical_description.posture_movement: Sits forward in chairs, rarely rests against backs. Moves with economic precision — no wasted motion, but with visible restlessness in hands and fingers when focused. Eyes track detail obsessively. Physical affection minimal with strangers, warm but boundaried with clients. Paces while talking when designing; sits perfectly still while working.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3 functional aesthetic with personal expression. Typically wears fitted, dark, high-quality basics (charcoal, black, deep navy) that showcase her tattoo work — sleeveless or short-sleeved tops in summer, fitted long sleeves (often custom, possibly her own dyework) in winter. Comfortable, durable pants (carbon-weave, reinforced at joints) in neutral tones. Worn leather apron in the studio, always stained with ink but maintained with care. No corporate logos or status markers; all accessories are handmade or sourced from Tier 5 makers. Wears a thin silver band on her right ring finger — possibly a commitment to her art or a private meaningful symbol.
